extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for academic journal referees on producing constructive, fair, and useful peer review comments that improve manuscripts and respect authors. Focuses on reviewer behavior, bias mitigation, tone, and practical advice for early-career reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid decision fatigue
rubrics_metrics.description: Review early in the day, one review per sitting, never when tired or hungry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule reviews when you have energy and focus to avoid rushed or inconsistent judgments; limit to one review per sitting to maintain quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of conscious and unconscious biases
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on facts not feelings, slow decision-making, root feedback in evidence; double-anonymized review helps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively check for both conscious and implicit biases when evaluating work; base critiques on evidence from the manuscript rather than impressions or assumptions; consider procedural safeguards (e.g., double-anonymized review) to reduce bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not treat null or negative results as grounds for rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Null or negative results aren't a basis for rejection — combat positive-results bias; evaluate on quality and methodology, not outcome favorability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess manuscripts according to methodological rigor, clarity, and contribution to knowledge irrespective of whether results are positive, null, or negative; avoid letting desired outcomes influence recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: List positives as well as negatives
rubrics_metrics.description: List positives as well as negatives — overly harsh reviews can cause authors to dismantle working sections; avoid sarcasm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin or balance reviews by highlighting strengths and useful elements of the manuscript; provide balanced critique to prevent authors from needlessly removing valuable content; maintain a professional, non-sarcastic tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give concrete examples and actionable advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Give concrete examples and advice — back opinions with specific manuscript instances; only recommend additions you would feasibly complete yourself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support critiques with precise citations of manuscript text (e.g., page, paragraph) and propose specific, actionable changes; refrain from suggesting extensive new work unless feasible, and avoid asking authors to do tasks you would do for them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek support when needed
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't be afraid to seek support — early-career reviewers can find mentors or co-reviewers for their first reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If inexperienced, request mentorship, co-reviewing, or editorial guidance to improve review quality; transparency with editors about co-reviewers or trained mentors is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the Golden Rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the Golden Rule — 'Would I be satisfied receiving this same review for my work?' If no, revise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use self-checking: imagine receiving your review as an author and adjust tone, thoroughness, and constructiveness accordingly; iterate until the review meets that standard.
